# How to Pick a Gemini Model and Check Which One Answered Your Question

> **In short:** In Gemini on a computer, you can choose a model from the model list, set how deeply it reasons, and check which model answered. Some models need an eligible Google AI plan, and Google's help center lists which plan includes what.

Have you ever asked an AI tool a hard question and felt the answer was too shallow? This guide shows you how to choose a Gemini model yourself, decide how much thinking it does, and confirm which model wrote your answer. It's for anyone with a personal Google Account who wants more control over Gemini. By the end, you'll know where each setting lives on a computer and what your plan allows.

## Before you start
- **A personal Google Account.** The steps below describe a personal account. Model availability is subject to change, so Google's official help center is the place to confirm the current details.
- **A Google AI plan, if you want to choose a specific model.** Google says some models are only available with paid Google AI plans. Without one, Gemini picks the model for you.
- **A computer with a web browser.** These steps follow Google's computer instructions. Phone screens can look different.
- **About 10 minutes.**

## Step 1 — Sign in and open Gemini on your computer
Open your web browser and go to gemini.google.com. Sign in with the personal Google Account you want to use. You should see Gemini's main screen, with a chat area in the middle and a message box near the bottom. If you have more than one Google account, make sure you pick the one connected to your Google AI plan, if you have one.

Nothing is sent to Gemini yet. You are only opening the screen where you will change the model. If the page looks different, for example because the layout has been updated, look for a chat or "new chat" option, or check Google's official help center, which has the current layouts. You'll know it worked when you can see a chat area and a message box at the bottom of the screen.

## Step 2 — Find the model label in the chat box
Start a new chat so your settings apply cleanly from your first message. Look at the bottom of the chat box, right where you would type. Near it, you will see the model that is currently selected. Google's help center explains that this is the model that will answer your next message, so this label is your check before you type.

Don't type anything yet. Just find the label and note which model is selected right now. If you don't see one, look for a small button or dropdown near the message box, since the layout changes over time. If nothing matches, the official help center has up-to-date instructions.

💬 Example: Don't type a question yet. Write down the model name shown at the bottom of the chat box.

You'll know it worked when you can point to the selected model's name at the bottom of the chat box.

## Step 3 — Open the model list and choose a model
Click the model label at the bottom of the chat box. A list of models opens. Google describes its models for different jobs: some are built for quick everyday answers, and others are designed for complex, multi-step problems. Read the short description next to each one and pick the one that fits your question. Click the model you want.

Some higher-tier models have a small lock icon next to them. Google says those require an eligible plan upgrade, so if you see a lock, your current plan doesn't include that model. Choose an unlocked model instead, or check the official help center for which plan includes which models. Your next message will go to the model you chose.

💬 Example: "I am planning a [trip length] trip to [destination] on a budget of [amount] and need a day-by-day plan."

Even a strong model can make mistakes, so double-check anything important, such as dates, numbers, or instructions you plan to follow. If the model you want is locked, pick another one and keep going. You'll know it worked when your answer appears and the chat box still shows the model you selected.

## Step 4 — Set the thinking level
Look for thinking levels near the model choice. Google lists three: Low, Medium, and High. Low gives fast, concise answers for straightforward questions. Medium balances speed and depth for everyday tasks. High lets the model reason carefully through complex, multi-step prompts. Pick the level that matches your question.

If you don't choose a level, Google says it defaults to Low. Higher levels usually take longer and use more of your plan's usage, so save High for problems that really need careful thought. Google also says that if you return to the same conversation later, Gemini keeps the model and thinking level you chose there.

💬 Example: "Compare two ways to pay off a [debt type] in [number] months, and explain each step in plain words."

If you can't find the thinking levels, look for a small menu near the model name, or check the official help center. You'll know it worked when the level you chose is shown before you send your question.

## Step 5 — Check which model answered
After you get a response, you may want to confirm which model wrote it. Google's help center says that on a computer, you can go to a chat from the sidebar, then click More at the bottom of a response. From the menu, select Show thinking steps. A panel shows the steps the model took.

Scroll to the bottom of those steps, and you will find which model was used. This matters because auto model selection can choose a model for you. Checking this is the most reliable way to know which model actually answered. If you don't see More or Show thinking steps, the menu may be labeled differently, so check the official help center.

💬 Example: After a response appears, click More, choose Show thinking steps, and scroll to the bottom to read the model name.

You'll know it worked when you can see the model name listed at the end of the thinking steps.

## Step 6 — Decide whether auto model selection should be on
Auto model selection lets Gemini choose the model and thinking level for each prompt. Google says it routes prompts to an efficient option to preserve your usage. If you want every answer to come from the model you picked, turn it off. On a computer, click Settings at the bottom left, open Usage limits, and at the bottom of that page, turn auto model selection on or off.

Turn it off if you want full control. Google says that when it's off, responses use a default fast model unless you have chosen another model in the chat. Also note that if you reach your plan's usage limit, Google says your chat continues with a faster model. Turn the setting back on whenever you'd rather Gemini decide.

💬 Example: No typing needed. Open Settings, then Usage limits, and read whether auto model selection is on or off.

You'll know it worked when the auto model selection switch shows the setting you chose.

## Common mistakes
- **Assuming your chosen model always answers.** Auto model selection can route prompts elsewhere. The fix is Step 5: check the thinking steps to see which model wrote the answer.
- **Choosing High thinking for every question.** Simple questions don't need deep reasoning, and higher levels use more of your usage. The fix is Low for quick questions and Medium or High for harder problems.
- **Expecting a locked model to open for free.** Google says higher-tier models marked with a lock need an eligible plan upgrade. The fix is to check the official help center for plan details, or pick an unlocked model.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** For a trip, a budget, or a study schedule, use a stronger model and a higher thinking level for the complicated parts, and a faster one for quick questions.
- **For your business or work:** If you use Gemini through a work or school account, Google says available models depend on that account's license. The steps here describe personal accounts, so check your account's options before you plan around a model.
- **If you're just getting started:** Keep the default settings, then try one harder question with a stronger model and Medium thinking. Compare how the answer changes.

## Try it now
Open gemini.google.com on your computer, find the model label at the bottom of the chat box, and note which model is selected. You'll know you're ready when you can say which model your next question will use.
